name: gh_raw
description:
Run an arbitrary gh command and return its result without raising.

Escape hatch for gh operations without a dedicated tool (e.g.
["release", "list", "--repo", "epik-agent/Epik"]). Pass arguments as a list
to avoid shell-quoting bugs; do not pass a single command string.

Args:
    args: The list of arguments passed to gh, excluding the leading "gh".

name: label_list
description:
List every label in a repository with its color and description.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.

name: label_create
description:
Create a label in a repository, or with force update an existing one.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.
    name: Label name.
    color: Hex color without the leading '#' (e.g. 'ff0000').
    description: Description of the label. Default "".
    force: Update the label if it already exists. Default false.

name: label_delete
description:
Delete a label from a repository.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.
    name: Label name.

name: run_list
description:
List a repository's GitHub Actions runs, newest first.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.
    workflow: Only runs of this workflow, by name or filename.
    branch: Only runs on this branch.
    status: Only runs with this status or conclusion (e.g. in_progress, failure).
    limit: Maximum number of runs. Default 20.

name: run_get
description:
Get one GitHub Actions run, with its event, head SHA and timestamps.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.
    run_id: The run's database ID.

name: run_logs
description:
Get the logs of a GitHub Actions run, of one of its jobs, or of only its failed steps.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.
    run_id: The run's database ID.
    job_id: Only this job's logs.
    failed_only: Only the failed steps' logs. Default false.

name: project_list
description:
List a GitHub user's or organization's open Projects.

Use this to find a project's number for the other project tools.

Args:
    owner: The user or organization login that owns the projects.

Returns a list of { number, title, url }.

name: project_list_items
description:
List the issues in a GitHub Project, optionally only those with one status.

Args:
    owner: The user or organization login that owns the project.
    number: The project number, from its URL or project_list.
    status_filter: If given, only items whose Status is this.

Returns a list of { issue_number, title, url, repo, status }.

name: project_get_item
description:
Get an issue's item in a GitHub Project, with its field values.

Args:
    owner: The user or organization login that owns the project.
    number: The project number, from its URL or project_list.
    repo: The issue's repository, as owner/name.
    issue_number: The issue number.

Returns { found: true, item_id, fields: { field name: value } }, or
{ found: false } when the issue is not in the project.

name: project_set_status
description:
Set an issue's Status in a GitHub Project, adding the issue to the project if it is not in it.

Args:
    owner: The user or organization login that owns the project.
    number: The project number, from its URL or project_list.
    repo: The issue's repository, as owner/name.
    issue_number: The issue number.
    status_name: The Status option, e.g. "In Progress" or "Done".

Returns { item_id, status }.

name: issue_set_blocked_by
description:
Mark an issue as blocked by another issue.

Args:
    repo: Repository of the blocked issue, in owner/name format.
    issue_number: The issue that is blocked.
    blocked_by_number: The issue that blocks it.
    blocked_by_repo: Repository of the blocking issue. Defaults to repo.

name: issue_remove_blocked_by
description:
Remove a blocked-by relationship between two issues.

Args:
    repo: Repository of the blocked issue, in owner/name format.
    issue_number: The issue that is blocked.
    blocked_by_number: The issue that blocks it.
    blocked_by_repo: Repository of the blocking issue. Defaults to repo.

name: issue_list_blocked_by
description:
List the issues blocking an issue.

Returns each blocking issue's url, number, title, state and repository.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.
    issue_number: The blocked issue.

name: epic_status
description:
Report the status of each sub-issue of an epic.

Issues and pull requests are named by URL, which holds their repository as
well as their number; sub-issues may be in other repositories.

For each sub-issue: url, number, title, state; linked_pr, the pull request in
its repository that references it (number, state, url); ci, the combined
check-run result on that pull request's head commit (failure, pending,
success, or null); blocked_by, the URLs of its blocking issues that are
sub-issues of the epic; and position, its level in the dependency graph (0
with no blockers, else one more than its deepest blocker). Issues on a
dependency cycle have position null, and each cycle is listed under the
top-level cycles key. When a read fails, its sub-issue has degraded: true and
errors, the failures, and the fields the read would fill are null or empty.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.
    epic_issue_number: The epic issue.

name: build_start
description:
Ask the Epik app to build a GitHub issue or epic, and return once the build has started.

This is how to implement an issue or an epic. Never implement one in this
conversation: when the user asks to build, implement or work on an issue or
an epic, call this tool.

The Epik app runs the build, and is started first if it isn't running. An
issue with sub-issues is built as an epic: the app runs its issues in
dependency order, one coding agent each, and merges each issue's pull
request into the epic branch itself; the epic's pull request into the
repository's default branch waits for the user to review and merge it. Any
other issue is built alone, and its pull request into the default branch
waits for the user. The user can watch the build from the Epik app's tray
icon, or with `tail -f` on the events log this returns.

Args:
    repo: Repository in owner/name format.
    number: The issue or epic issue to build.
    branch: The branch the pull requests merge into. Default
        epic/<number>-<slug of its title> for an epic, and the repository's
        default branch for an issue.

Returns run_id (the run, owner/name#number: the epic issue), build_id (this
build, one attempt at the run), kind (epic or issue), branch, build_dir (the
build's record) and events (the build's events log, in build_dir). Building
an epic again after a failure or an interruption adds a build to its run, and
the run's time and cost add up across its builds.

name: build_status
description:
Ask the Epik app where a run is: its state, its builds, and each of its issues'.

The app isn't started: when it isn't running, this says so.

Args:
    run_id: The run, owner/name#number, as build_start or build_list gives it.

Returns the run's repo, number, title, kind (epic or issue), branch,
disposition (building, waiting_for_review or needs_attention), reason (why it
needs attention), pull_request, started_at, latest_at, and elapsed_ms and
cost_usd summed over its builds; its builds, oldest first, each with
build_id, status (running, succeeded, failed or interrupted), reason,
pull_request, started_at, ended_at, elapsed_ms and cost_usd; and its issues:
each issue's number, title, blocked_by, status (waiting, running, succeeded,
merged, failed or closed), reason, pull_request, merge_commit, and
duration_ms and cost_usd summed over its builds, and for a running issue its
activity: last_action, last_test, last_event and its recent actions.

name: build_list
description:
List the Epik app's runs, newest activity first.

The app isn't started: when it isn't running, this says so.

Args:
    limit: Maximum number of runs. Default 20.

Returns each run's state, as build_status gives it.
